docs.title: Official TicketForge Docs
docs.text:
The command center for your Discord community. Tame the chaos with intuitive ticket panels, smart automation, and powerful application forms.

Get Started View Premium

docs.title: Powerful Management
docs.text:
TicketForge isn't just a bot, it's a full CRM for Discord.

  • Data-Driven Decisions

    Visualize your support health with the Guild Statistics dashboard. Track ticket volume, response times, and peak hours to optimize your staffing.

  • Web Portal Applications

    Share direct links to your forms. Users can apply via a beautiful external web interface, with responses syncing directly to your dashboard and Discord server.

  • Audit Logs

    Never lose track of a change. The Activity Log provides a detailed timeline of every configuration update, submission review, and dashboard login.

  • CSAT & Analytics

    Gather CSAT scores (1-5 Stars) and feedback after every ticket. Use this data to identify your top-performing support agents.

docs.title: Premium Subscription
docs.text:
TicketForge operates on a generous Freemium model. The core features needed to run a support system are free forever.

Premium is designed for power users, large communities, and professional teams who need advanced automation, deeper insights, and complete brand control.

docs.title: 1. Purchase Subscription
docs.text: Support the development directly via our Dashboard. * Monthly: €5.00/mo * Yearly: €50.00/yr (Save 20%)

docs.title: 2. Vote to Earn (Free)
docs.text:
You can earn temporary Premium access by voting for TicketForge on top.gg.

  1. Run the /vote command in your server.
  2. Click the link to vote.
  3. Reward: receive Tokens for every vote.
    • Votes are cumulative. Vote daily to keep Premium active for free!

docs.title: 1. Scale without Limits
docs.text: The free plan is generously capped to handle normal server loads. Premium unlocks huge capacities: * Tickets: 25 Panels (Up from 3) * Applications: 15 Applications (Up from 3)

docs.title: 2. Advanced Application Forms
docs.text: Unleash the full power of the form builder for your recruitment and appeals: * Image Uploads: Require users to upload screenshots (e.g., proof of bans, portfolio). * Regex Validation: Enforce strict formatting (e.g., email addresses or specific ID formats) on text answers. * Time Limits: Apply a countdown timer to applications. Perfect for tests or strict questionnaires. * Advanced Web Portals: Force Discord sign-in, allow anonymous submissions, and enable pre-submit answer modifications.

docs.title: 3. Professional Ticket Automation
docs.text: Stop doing manual work. Premium automates the boring stuff: * Escalation: Move tickets seamlessly between departments (e.g., Support -> Billing). * Google Drive Sync: Automatically upload transcripts to your cloud storage. * Auto-Close: Automatically close tickets if the user leaves the server.

docs.title: 4. Custom Branding
docs.text:
Make the bot feel like your bot.

  • Nickname, Avatar & Banner: Customize the bot's appearance in your server.
  • Server Bio: Set a custom "About Me" visible in the bot's profile.
  • Whitelabel (Custom Bot): Run the bot under your own token with your own name and avatar — exclusive to the Support Plan.
  • Clean Footers: Remove "Powered by TicketForge" from embeds.

docs.title: Role Automation & Triggers
docs.text:
Stop manually updating Discord roles every time an application is processed. TicketForge can handle role assignments, edge cases, and staff reminders automatically.

The automation options on the automation settings page.

Navigate to Edit Application > Automation to configure these settings.

docs.title: 1. Resolution Actions
docs.text:
You can instruct the bot to add or remove specific Discord roles based on the exact status of the application.

  • On Submit: Executes the moment a user finishes the form (e.g., adding an "Applicant" role so they know their form went through).
  • On Accept: Executes when a staff member approves the application (e.g., adding the "Trial Mod" role and removing the "Applicant" role).
  • On Deny: Safely revert or remove roles if the user is rejected.

Configure role additions and removals for each stage of the application.

Permission Check

For the bot to assign these roles, the TicketForge role must be placed higher in your Discord Server Settings than the roles you select here.

docs.title: 2. Auto-Deny Missing Users (Premium)
docs.text:
Sometimes users apply for a position and then leave the server before your staff has a chance to review their submission.

If Auto-Deny Missing Users is enabled, TicketForge will automatically detect if the applicant is no longer in the Discord server. It will instantly mark their pending application as "Denied" and log it, keeping your staff queue clean from ghost applications.

Automatically clean up your queue if an applicant leaves the server.

docs.title: 3. Inactivity Notifier (Premium)
docs.text: Never let an application slip through the cracks. The Inactivity Notifier will automatically ping your staff if an application sits in the "Pending" state for too long.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Notification Channel: The text channel where the reminder ping should be sent (usually a private staff channel).
  2. Roles to Ping: Select your Management or Reviewer roles.
  3. Initial Delay: The amount of time the application must sit idle before the first ping is sent (e.g., 24 hours).

docs.title: Repeating Reminders
docs.text:
If a single ping isn't enough to get your staff's attention, you can enable Repeating Reminders. * Interval Time: Continue to ping staff every X hours. * Max Pings: Limit how many times the reminder repeats (e.g., stop pinging after 3 reminders) to prevent endless spam if the team is genuinely busy.

Configure smart, repeating reminders to ensure applications are reviewed promptly.

docs.title: Creating an Application
docs.text: An Application allows you to collect structured data from your users through dynamic forms. TicketForge allows you to build multiple applications for different purposes (e.g., "Staff Recruitment", "Ban Appeals", "Giveaway Entry").

docs.title: 1. Login & Access
docs.text:
To begin, visit the TicketForge Website.

  1. Click the Login with Discord button in the top right corner.
  2. Authorize the TicketForge application to access your account information.

The main dashboard landing page.

docs.title: 2. Server Selection
docs.text:
Once logged in, you will automatically navigate to the server selection page. Select the server where you want to create the application.

You can also navigate to this page by clicking on your profile and then "Servers".

  1. Click on your Profile Picture in the top right corner to open the menu.
  2. Select Dashboard from the dropdown menu.

Your available servers list.

Can't see your server?

If a server is missing from this list, ensure you have the Manage Server permission on that Discord server. If you just got permissions, try logging out and logging back in to refresh your token.

docs.title: 3. Creating the Application
docs.text:
After selecting a server, navigate to the Applications tab in the sidebar and click the Create Application card.

Click the card with the plus icon to begin.

docs.title: Step A: Selection Strategy
docs.text:
You will be presented with three ways to start your configuration:

  1. Official Templates (): Pre-configured templates designed by our team for common use cases (e.g., "Staff Recruitment").
  2. Community Templates (): User-generated templates shared by other server owners.
  3. Import from Code (): If you have a share code (format: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX), paste it here to clone an exact configuration.

Select a template, browse by category, or import a code to proceed.

docs.title: Previewing Templates
docs.text:
Before making a choice, you can click on any template card to open a detailed Interactive Preview. This allows you to view the exact questions, the Discord embed message, and the user flow before committing to it.

Preview the questions and visual layout before selecting a template.

docs.title: Step B: Configuration
docs.text:
Once you click Use Template, you must configure the core identity of the application.

You only need to define three essential settings: * Application Name: The title of the form (e.g., "Moderator Application"). * Target Results Channel: The private Discord channel where completed application answers will be posted for your staff to read. (Required) * Review Roles (Optional): The Discord roles (e.g., @Head Mod) that are allowed to click the "Accept" or "Deny" buttons on the submitted applications.

The setup wizard ensures your application routes to the right channel.

docs.title: Step C: Creation
docs.text:
Click Create Application. You will be instantly redirected to the Application Editor where you can finalize your questions, adjust automation rules, and send the form to your Discord server!

Your application is created and ready for final edits.

docs.title: Delivery & Web Portals
docs.text:
How do users actually fill out your application? You can configure this under Edit Application > General Settings.

The delivery method selector on the general settings page.

docs.title: Application Methods
docs.text: Method Description Direct Message (DM) The bot sends the form to the user's DMs. (Requires users to have server DMs enabled). Web Portal Generates a secure, shareable web link (e.g., ticketforge.xyz/apply/...) that users can fill out in their browser. Both Allows the user to choose their preferred method when they click the trigger button in your server.

docs.title: Web Portal Features
docs.text:
If you use the Web Portal method, you gain access to several powerful tools tailored for browser-based submissions:

  • Require Discord Sign-in: (Premium) Forces users to log in with Discord before viewing the form, preventing link forwarding to non-members.
  • Allow Anonymous Submissions: (Premium) Collect raw feedback without attaching a Discord account identity. (Anonymous submissions cannot be formally "Accepted" or "Denied" as there is no user to notify).

docs.title: The Application Editor
docs.text:
The Application Editor is your workspace for building and refining your forms. It features a real-time health check system, auto-save protection, and granular control over every aspect of your application workflow.

The Application Editor view with the settings grid and action toolbar.

docs.title: Editor Navigation
docs.text: The application settings are divided into logical categories to help you build your form step-by-step:

docs.title: 1. General & Visuals
docs.text:
• General — Rename the app, toggle its Active status, update the Target Results Channel, and select the Apply Method (DM, Web Portal, or Both).
  • Layout — Switch between standard buttons, dropdown menus, or multi-app layouts.
  • Questions — The core Form Builder. Add, edit, reorder, or set time limits on your questions.
  • Buttons — Customize the color, label, and emoji of the button users click to start the app.
  • Messages — Customize the text and embeds sent by the bot (Start Notice, Success Message, DM results, etc.).

docs.title: 2. Advanced & Automation
docs.text:
Powerful tools to restrict access and automate your workflow.

  • Access & Limits — Restrict applications to specific roles, set cooldowns, and cap pending applications.
  • Automation — Auto-assign roles when an application is submitted, accepted, or denied.
  • Audit Logging — Post updates to a private channel when users start, submit, or cancel forms.
  • Integrations (Premium) — Run the application under your own Custom Bot identity.

docs.title: Health Check (Status Badge)
docs.text:
In the top right toolbar, you will see a live App Health badge. * 🟢 Healthy: The application is ready to use. * 🟡 Warnings: Non-critical issues found (e.g., "No Review Roles selected"). * 🔴 Critical: Errors that prevent the app from working (e.g., "Missing Target Results Channel").

Click the badge to see a detailed checklist. Clicking on an issue will automatically scroll you to the exact setting that needs fixing.

The App Health dropdown helps you quickly spot configuration errors.

docs.title: Save System
docs.text:
The editor tracks your changes locally. If you modify any setting, a Save Bar appears at the bottom of the screen. * Discard: Reverts all unsaved changes to the last stable version. * Save Changes: Pushes your configuration to the database and the live bot.

The savebar.

Idle Protection

If you leave the editor open without saving, an "Idle" modal will appear to prevent data loss or conflicting edits.

docs.title: Action Menu
docs.text:
Located in the top toolbar, these quick-actions allow you to deploy and manage the application itself.

The actionbar on the paneleditor page. Action Icon Description Send to Discord Posts the configured trigger message/button to a channel of your choice. Update in Discord Updates the content/embeds of an existing application message without deleting it. Share Code Generates a XXXX-XXXX-XXXX code to safely share this configuration with another server. Clone Creates an exact duplicate of this application within the same server. Template Publishes this configuration to the Community Templates gallery. Rename Change the internal name of the application. Delete Permanently removes the application configuration. Cannot be undone.

docs.title: Interaction Styles (Layouts)
docs.text:
TicketForge gives you total control over how users start your applications. Instead of cluttering your server with dozens of different buttons across multiple channels, you can combine applications into sleek, unified menus.

Panel with dropdown selection.

Navigate to Edit Application > Layout to choose and configure your interaction style.

docs.title: 1. Standard Button
docs.text:
The default layout. A single button attached to an embed message that triggers one specific application.

  • Best for: Dedicated channels (e.g., a #staff-applications channel that only serves one purpose).
  • Customization: You can change the button's text, color, and emoji from the Buttons tab.

docs.title: 2. Select Menu (Dropdown)
docs.text:
Combines multiple applications into a clean dropdown menu. When a user selects an option, the assigned application instantly opens.

  • Capacity: Up to 5 options (Free) or 25 options (Premium).
  • Best for: Hub channels where users need to choose from many different types of forms (e.g., "Report Player", "Report Bug", "Ban Appeal").

Panel with dropdown selection.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Menu Placeholder: The grey text visible before a user clicks the menu (e.g., "Choose an application...").
  2. Add Options: Click Add New Option.
  3. Label & Description: Define what the user sees in the list.
  4. Trigger Application: Select which existing application opens when this option is clicked.

docs.title: 3. Multi-Panel (Button Grid)
docs.text:
Attaches multiple applications as individual buttons stacked under a single embed message.

  • Capacity: Up to 5 buttons (Free) or 15 buttons (Premium).
  • Best for: Small to medium hubs where you want all options immediately visible without requiring the user to click a dropdown first (e.g., "Apply for Mod" and "Apply for Builder" side-by-side).

Panel with multiple buttons.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Attached Applications: Select which applications to include from the multi-select dropdown.
  2. Buttons Per Row: Control the grid layout. Discord allows a maximum of 5 buttons per row. If you attach 6 applications and set "Buttons Per Row" to 3, you will get a perfect 3x2 grid.

Live Preview

The Layout page features a Live Preview box at the top. As you add dropdown items or adjust your multi-panel grid, the preview updates instantly so you know exactly how it will look in Discord!

docs.title: Access Limits & Cooldowns
docs.text:
Protect your staff from spam by restricting who can apply and how often.

Navigate to Edit Application > Access & Limits to configure your server's defense mechanisms.

The limits configurator on the limits settings page.

docs.title: 1. Role Restrictions
docs.text:
Strictly define which Discord roles are permitted to view and start the application.

  • Required Roles: The user MUST have one of these roles to see the application button. Useful for restricting forms to "Level 10+" or "VIP" members.
  • Blocked Roles: The user is prevented from applying if they have ANY of these roles. This is perfect for blocking "Muted", "Blacklisted", or "Suspended" roles from spamming the system.

Control exactly who can and cannot interact with your application.

docs.title: 2. Quantity Limits
docs.text:
Cap the volume of applications to ensure your staff isn't overwhelmed.

  • Per User Limit: Restrict users from having more than X pending applications at once. Usually, this is set to 1 to prevent a single user from submitting multiple identical forms.
  • Global Limit: Cap the total number of unreviewed applications server-wide. If this limit is reached, nobody else can apply until staff reviews the existing backlog.

Prevent application spam by capping pending submissions.

docs.title: 3. Submission Cooldowns (Premium)
docs.text:
Even if a user's previous application was reviewed and denied, you might not want them instantly applying again.

Enable the Submission Cooldown to force users to wait a specific amount of time (e.g., 7 days or 30 days) after submitting before they are allowed to apply for this specific form again.

Force users to wait between application attempts.

docs.title: 4. Time Constraints
docs.text:
You can apply a countdown timer to the entire application process. This is excellent for exams, trivia, or ensuring users don't hold an application "open" for days at a time.

  1. Application Time Limit: Set the maximum allowed time (in minutes or hours) to complete the entire form.
    • Note: You can also set specific time limits on individual questions via the Questions tab.
  2. Auto-Submit on Timeout: (Premium) If the timer runs out, you can automatically submit whatever answers the user did finish instead of immediately discarding the application.
  3. Auto-Submit Min %: If Auto-Submit is enabled, you can require the user to have completed at least X% of the form for it to save. If they complete less than the minimum percentage when the timer expires, the application is discarded.

Apply strict time limits and auto-submission logic to your forms.

docs.title: Audit Logging
docs.text:
Keep a strict, tamper-proof paper trail of your applicants and staff actions. Instead of digging through Discord's default audit logs, TicketForge can route specific application lifecycle events to a dedicated channel.

Navigate to Edit Application > Audit Logging to configure your event stream.

The logging configurator on the logging settings page.

docs.title: 1. Setup
docs.text:
To begin logging, simply select a private Audit Log Channel from the dropdown menu.

Once a channel is selected, the bot will post detailed, color-coded embeds into this channel whenever a significant event occurs. Each log entry includes: * The exact timestamp of the event. * The targeted user (the applicant). * The staff member who executed the action (if applicable). * The Application ID for easy cross-referencing in the dashboard.

Select a private channel to act as your application audit log.

docs.title: 2. Loggable Events
docs.text:
By default, some servers don't want to be pinged for every tiny action. You can toggle specific events ON or OFF to reduce spam in your log channel:

Event Description Started Logs the exact moment a user clicks the trigger button and begins the form. Useful for tracking drop-off rates. Submitted Logs when a user successfully finishes the final question and submits the application. Approved Logs when a staff member officially Accepts the application. Denied Logs when a staff member officially Rejects the application. Cancelled Logs if a user manually aborts the process, or if their time limit expires before they can submit.

Toggle specific lifecycle events to keep your log channel clean and relevant.

docs.title: Messages & Embeds
docs.text:
Because applications have a multi-stage lifecycle, the bot needs to communicate with users and staff at various points. Under Edit Application > Messages, you can fully customize every single touchpoint.

The Messages Editor features a split layout: select a message on the left, and visually edit it on the right.

docs.title: 1. Message Categories
docs.text: The left sidebar categorizes all available messages into three logical groups based on when they are sent.

docs.title: User Flow
docs.text: Messages that the applicant sees while interacting with your form. * Main Panel Message: The public message sent to your server containing the "Start Application" button. * Start Notice: Sent to the user before they begin the form. Great for listing requirements or rules. * Application Started: Confirms the form has begun and provides instructions. * Pre-Submit Confirmation: The final "Are you sure?" prompt shown before their answers are permanently submitted. * Application Submitted: The success embed shown to the user after completion.

docs.title: Staff Review
docs.text: Messages sent to your private staff channels. * Application Received: The embed posted to your Target Results Channel. This contains the user's details and all their answers. * Review Result: (Premium) Automatically updates the original "Application Received" message to show which staff member accepted or denied it. * Inactivity Notifier: (Premium) The reminder ping sent to staff if an application is ignored for too long.

docs.title: Results (DMs)
docs.text: Automated direct messages sent to the user after a staff member makes a decision. * Accepted Notice: (Premium) Sent to the user's DMs when approved. * Denied Notice: (Premium) Sent to the user's DMs when rejected.

docs.title: 2. The Visual Builder
docs.text:
When you select a message, the right pane opens the Canvas Editor alongside a Live Preview.

  1. Live Preview: Instantly updates to show exactly how your message will look in Discord.
  2. Content & Embeds: You can send plain text, or construct rich embeds with titles, descriptions, custom colors, and fields.
  3. Images: Add a custom thumbnail or large image to make your messages stand out.

Build professional embeds using the visual Canvas Editor.

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Placeholders
docs.text:
Make your messages feel personalized by using Placeholders. Click the Placeholders button in the bottom right of the Live Preview to see all available variables.

  • User Variables: Mention the applicant with {user_mention} or display their name with {user_name}.
  • Application Variables: Reference the application by name using {app_name}.
  • Form Answers: You can insert the user's exact answers directly into the Staff Review messages using {form_answer_1}, {form_answer_2}, etc.
  • Review Data: In your DM Result messages, use {review_reason} to automatically insert the exact reason the staff member typed when they clicked Accept or Deny.

Use placeholders to inject dynamic data into your text and embeds.

docs.title: Inactivity Notifier
docs.text:
(Premium Feature)

Never let an application slip through the cracks. The Inactivity Notifier acts as a smart alarm clock for your staff. If an application sits in the "Pending" state for too long without being reviewed, the bot will automatically send a reminder ping to your team.

Navigate to Edit Application > Automation to configure your notifier settings.

The notifications configurator on the automation settings page.

docs.title: 1. Basic Configuration
docs.text:
To enable the notifier, you need to define where the alert goes and who it pings:

  1. Enable Inactivity Notifier: Toggle the master switch to ON.
  2. Notification Channel: Select the text channel where the reminder ping should be sent. This is usually a private #staff-chat or #management channel.
  3. Roles to Ping: Select the specific Discord roles (e.g., @Reviewer or @Admin) that should be mentioned in the alert.
  4. Initial Delay: The amount of time the application must sit idle before the first ping is sent (e.g., 24 hours).

Set up the channel, roles, and initial delay for your reminders.

docs.title: 2. Repeating Reminders
docs.text:
If your team is busy, a single ping might get lost in the chat. You can enable Repeating Reminders to have the bot continuously follow up until a staff member finally clicks Accept or Deny.

  • Interval Time: The amount of time the bot should wait between consecutive pings (e.g., every 12 hours).
  • Max Pings: Limit how many times the reminder repeats. For example, setting this to 3 means the bot will stop pinging after the 3rd reminder, preventing endless spam if your team is genuinely unavailable.

Configure the interval and maximum ping limits for repeating alerts.

Workflow Synergy

The Inactivity Notifier pairs perfectly with the Auto-Deny Missing Users feature. If an applicant leaves the server while sitting in the queue, the application is auto-denied, and the Inactivity Notifier is safely canceled so your staff isn't pinged for a dead application!

docs.title: Question Builder
docs.text:
The core of any application is the data you collect. The Question Builder is a powerful, drag-and-drop interface that lets you design the exact form your users will fill out.

Navigate to Edit Application > Questions to open the builder.

The Question Builder interface featuring drag-and-drop ordering and live previews.

docs.title: 1. Managing Questions
docs.text:
• Add a Question: Click the Add New Question button at the bottom of the list. You can add up to 10 questions on the Free plan, or 25 on Premium.
  • Reorder: Click and hold the grip icon () on the left side of any question to drag it up or down the list.
  • Expand/Collapse: Click anywhere on a question's header to open its configuration settings.

docs.title: 2. Basic Properties
docs.text:
Every question, regardless of its type, shares these core settings:

  • Question Label: The actual prompt the user sees (e.g., "Why do you want to join the team?").
  • Description / Help Text: Smaller, secondary text used to provide context or instructions (e.g., "Please provide at least two sentences.").
  • Required Response: If toggled ON, the user cannot submit the application without answering this question. If toggled OFF, it becomes optional.

docs.title: 3. Response Types
docs.text: TicketForge supports multiple ways for users to answer your questions. Select the Response Type at the top of the expanded question menu.

docs.title: Text Answer
docs.text:
The standard text input box. * Min / Max Characters: Enforce strict length limits. Prevent one-word answers by setting a minimum character count, or prevent spam by capping the maximum length. * Regex Validation: (Premium) Require the answer to match a specific mathematical pattern. Perfect for forcing users to enter valid email addresses, URLs, or specific ID formats.

Configuring character limits and validation for a text response.

docs.title: Multiple Choice
docs.text:
Provide users with a list of predefined options to choose from. * Add Choices: Click Add Choice to create new options. You can have up to 5 choices (Free) or 25 choices (Premium) per question. * Min / Max Selections: This setting dictates how the question behaves: * Radio Buttons (Single Choice): Set Min to 1 and Max to 1. The user can only pick one answer. * Checkboxes (Multiple Choice): Set Max to a number greater than 1. The user can select multiple options simultaneously.

Building a multiple-choice question with minimum and maximum selection limits.

docs.title: Image Upload (Premium)
docs.text:
Requires the user to provide an image attachment. * Best for: Age verification, building portfolios, or providing screenshot proof for ban appeals. * Note: Users will be prompted to upload a file directly from their device or paste an image URL.

Building a multiple-choice question with minimum and maximum selection limits.

docs.title: 4. Time Constraints (Premium)
docs.text:
Want to run a timed test or a strict questionnaire where users can't spend hours Googling answers? You can enforce a strict Time Limit on individual questions.

  1. Toggle Time Limit to ON at the bottom of the question configuration.
  2. Set the Duration (e.g., 60 seconds).
  3. When the user reaches this question, a visible countdown timer will appear. If it hits zero, the question is locked, and they are forced to move to the next one.

docs.title: Processing Submissions
docs.text:
When users complete an application, their answers are sent to two places simultaneously: your Target Results Channel in Discord, and your web dashboard.

While you can review applications entirely within Discord using the buttons attached to the application embeds, the Submissions Dashboard provides a powerful, unified inbox for your staff to manage high volumes of applicants.

docs.title: 1. The Submissions Inbox
docs.text:
Navigate to Submissions on the dashboard sidebar to view all applications across your server.

The Submissions Dashboard allows you to search and filter applications.

docs.title: Filtering & Searching
docs.text: Use the top control bar to quickly find what you're looking for: * Search: Look up a specific user by their Discord Username or User ID. * Panel Filter: Only show submissions from a specific application (e.g., only show "Builder Applications"). * Status Filter: Filter by lifecycle state: * Pending: Awaiting review. * Interviewing: Pushed to a secondary stage. * Accepted / Denied: Resolved applications. * Date Range: Filter submissions from the last 7 days, 30 days, or a custom range.

docs.title: 2. Viewing Application Details
docs.text:
Clicking on any submission card opens the Details Modal, giving you complete context before making a decision.

The Details Modal displays applicant history and their answers.

docs.title: Applicant Profile & History
docs.text: At the top of the modal, you'll see the user's avatar, Discord ID, and a historical summary. This helps you identify serial applicants or users who have been repeatedly denied in the past. Displays their Total, Pending, Interviewing, Accepted, and Denied counts.

docs.title: Applicant Answers
docs.text: Scroll down to view exactly how the user answered your form. * Text Answers: Displayed in easily readable blocks. * Multiple Choice: Displayed as clean, tagged pills. * Image Uploads: Rendered directly in the dashboard so you don't have to open external links to verify proof or portfolios.

docs.title: 3. Moderation Actions
docs.text: As a staff member (with a designated Review Role), you can finalize the application using the action buttons.

docs.title: Accept or Deny
docs.text:
Clicking Accept or Deny will open a confirmation prompt requiring a Reason. * This reason is logged for your internal records. * If you have Result DMs configured, this reason is directly messaged to the applicant. * Any configured Role Automation (e.g., giving them the "Staff" role) triggers instantly upon confirmation.

Provide a reason when accepting or denying an application.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text: Permanently wipes the submission from the database. Use this for spam or test applications. This action is irreversible.

docs.title: Anonymous Submissions
docs.text: If your application allows Anonymous Submissions (common for feedback forms), the submission will be marked with a special ANONYMOUS badge. Because there is no Discord account attached to the submission, you cannot Accept or Deny anonymous forms. They are strictly read-only data for your team.

docs.title: 4. Discord Integration
docs.text:
You don't have to use the web dashboard! TicketForge is deeply integrated into Discord.

When a user submits an application, the bot posts an embed in your Target Results Channel containing their answers and attached Staff Action Buttons (Accept, Deny, Open Interview, User History).

Your staff can click these buttons directly inside Discord to trigger the exact same moderation modals and automations as the web dashboard.

docs.title: Automation
docs.text:
TicketForge can perform automated actions to help maintain your server's hygiene and keep users informed.

Automation settings.

docs.title: User Leave Handling
docs.text:
What happens if a user opens a ticket and then leaves the server?

  • Close Ticket: The ticket status changes to "Closed". The transcript is saved (if enabled), and staff can review it later.
  • Delete Ticket: The channel is immediately deleted. No transcript is saved.

docs.title: Automated DMs
docs.text:
The bot can send Direct Messages (DMs) to the user based on ticket events.

  • On Creation: "Your ticket #123 has been created in Server Name."
  • On Close: "Your ticket has been closed by Staff. If you need more help, please open a new ticket."

Privacy Settings

If a user has DMs disabled for your server, the bot will not be able to send these notifications. This is a Discord limitation.

docs.title: Ticket Claiming System
docs.text:
The Claiming System allows a staff member to take ownership of a ticket, preventing multiple moderators from responding to the same user simultaneously.

Claim settings.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Go to Panel Editor > Claiming to enable this feature.

docs.title: Behavior Rules
docs.text:
• Restrict Actions: If enabled, only the staff member who claimed the ticket (and the user) can type or use buttons. Other staff are locked out.
  • Claimer Must Unclaim: Prevents other staff from "stealing" a ticket. Only the original claimer can release it.
  • Zero Permissions: You can configure the bot to Hide the channel from other staff members once it is claimed.

docs.title: Visual Indicators
docs.text:
• Channel Rename: Change the channel name to claimed-{user}.
  • Category Move: Move the ticket to a specific "In Progress" category.

docs.title: Ticket Escalation
docs.text:
Escalation allows you to move an active ticket from one panel to another (e.g., from "General Support" to "Billing" or "High Priority"). This ensures tickets reach the right department without forcing the user to open a new request.

Escalation configuration settings.

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text: When a ticket is escalated: 1. The ticket adopts the configuration of the Target Panel. 2. Permissions are updated to match the new panel's Support Roles. 3. The ticket can be physically moved to a new Category. 4. Staff can be automatically unclaimed to allow the new team to take over.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Navigate to Panel Editor > Escalation.

docs.title: 1. Allowed Targets
docs.text: Select which panels this current panel can escalate to. * Example: A "Triage" panel might be allowed to escalate to "Billing", "Tech Support", and "Management".

docs.title: 2. Escalation Actions
docs.text:
Control what happens during the transfer:

Setting Description Update Category Moves the ticket channel to the category defined in the Target Panel. Update Permissions Syncs channel permissions to the Target Panel's support roles (e.g., hiding it from Moderators and showing it to Admins). Update Name Renames the channel based on the Target Panel's naming scheme. Auto Unclaim Removes the current claimer, releasing the ticket for the new department to claim. Send Transfer Message Posts a system message indicating the ticket has been transferred. Send New Panel Message Posts the "Welcome Message" of the target panel, ensuring the user sees the correct greeting/instructions for the new department.

docs.title: How to Escalate
docs.text:
Staff members can escalate a ticket in two ways:

  1. Escalation Button: If Show Escalate Button is enabled in settings, a button appears in the ticket interface.
  2. Slash Command: Using /escalate (if available) to select the target panel from a dropdown.

docs.title: Custom Forms (Modals)
docs.text:
Instead of creating a ticket immediately, you can require users to fill out a form (Modal) first. This helps your team get context before starting the conversation.

Form editor.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Panel Editor > Forms.
  2. Toggle Enable Ticket Forms.
  3. Click Add Question.

docs.title: Question Types
docs.text:
When creating a question, you can choose the Response Type (Text Input, Single Choice for radio buttons, or Multiple Choice for checkboxes). Depending on the type you select, different settings will be available:

Setting Applicable To Description Question Label All The question text (e.g., "What is your Minecraft Username?"). Required Response All Users cannot submit the form without answering this field. Available Options Single & Multiple Choice Define the choices users can pick from. You can add a main label and an optional description for each choice. Min/Max Selections Multiple Choice Enforce how many checkboxes a user must or can select. Placeholder Text Input Grey text inside the input box to guide the user. Multi-line Text Input Switches from a small input box to a large text area (Paragraph). Min/Max Length Text Input Enforce character limits for answers.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: When a user submits the form: 1. The ticket is created. 2. The bot posts an embed containing all their answers. 3. (Optional) Staff can edit these answers later if needed.

docs.title: Limits & Schedules
docs.text:
Control the flow of tickets to prevent spam and burnout.

Limit and Schedule settings.

docs.title: Ticket Limits
docs.text:
Prevent users from spamming your support team.

  • Per User Limit (open): Max open tickets a single user can have (Default: 1).
  • Per User Limit (closed): Max closed tickets a single user can have (Default: 500).
  • Bypass Roles: Select roles (like VIPs or Boosters) that ignore these limits.

docs.title: Operational Schedule
docs.text:
Define your support hours. Users cannot open tickets outside these times.

  1. Timezone: Select your team's timezone (e.g., America/New_York or UTC).
  2. Weekly Grid: Click blocks to toggle hours Open/Closed.
  3. Action:
    • Disable Creation: The button stops working.
    • Notification: The button works, but sends a custom "We are closed" message instead of the standard welcome.

docs.title: Staff Rating System (CSAT)
docs.text:
Gather feedback on your support team's performance.

Rating settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. A staff member closes the ticket.
  2. The bot sends a Rating Request (Embed with 1-5 Star buttons).
  3. The user clicks a star rating.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• Delivery Method:
    • Channel: Posts the request in the ticket before deletion.
    • DM: Sends the request to the user's Direct Messages.
    • Hybrid: Tries DM first, falls back to Channel if DMs are closed.
  • Public Feed: Select a channel to publicly post positive reviews as social proof.

docs.title: Tickets as Threads
docs.text:
By default, TicketForge creates a new Text Channel for every ticket. The Tickets as Threads feature changes this behavior to create Private Threads inside a single parent channel.

Ticket as thread settings.

docs.title: Why use Threads?
docs.text:
• Cleaner Sidebar: Prevents your server sidebar from getting cluttered with 50+ open ticket channels.
  • Bypass Limits: Discord has a limit of 500 channels per server. Threads do not count towards this limit, allowing for thousands of tickets.
  • Performance: Faster creation times on large servers.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Panel Editor > Threads.
  2. Enable Tickets as Threads.
  3. Parent Channel: Select the text channel where the threads will live.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Setting Description Thread Name Format: ticket-{count} or help-{user}. Add Support Team Automatically adds the configured support roles to the thread so they can view it. Allow User Invites Allows the ticket creator to invite other users to the thread via @mention.

Category Settings

When Thread Mode is enabled, Category settings are disabled. Threads always reside in their parent channel and cannot be "moved" to a category.

docs.title: Transcripts & Logging
docs.text:
TicketForge ensures you never lose the context of a conversation. Transcripts are permanent HTML files containing the full chat history.

Limit and Schedule settings.

docs.title: Cloud Backup (Google Drive)
docs.text:
Stop relying on Discord file attachments. You can sync transcripts directly to Google Drive.

  • Permanent Storage: Files in Discord may eventually become unavailable; Google Drive is yours forever.
  • Organization: Transcripts are uploaded and can be organized by date or ticket ID.

To enable this, visit Server Settings > Google Drive in the dashboard.

docs.title: Transcript Archiving
docs.text: Navigate to Panel Editor > Transcripts.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Storage Channel: Select a private text channel where the bot will post transcript files.
  2. Auto-Save: Automatically generate a transcript when a ticket is closed.
    • Trigger: Choose to save on Close (archive state) or Delete (permanent removal).
  3. DM Transcript: Send the HTML file directly to the user who opened the ticket.
    • Note: This will fail if the user has DMs disabled.

docs.title: Event Audit Log
docs.text: Separate from the chat history, the Audit Log tracks lifecycle events.

docs.title: Logged Events
docs.text:
You can toggle specific events to reduce spam: * Created / Closed / Reopened * Renamed * Deleted * Archived

Each log entry includes the Executor (who did it), the Target (ticket owner), and a timestamp.

docs.title: Dashboard Overview
docs.text: The TicketForge Dashboard is the command center for your support system. TicketForge provides a modern, responsive web interface to visualize and configure everything.

docs.title: 2. The Dashboard
docs.text:
Once you select a server, the Sidebar becomes your main navigation tool. It is divided into logical sections to help you manage different aspects of the bot.

The Panel Editor view with the sidebar navigation on the left. Section Description Panel Editor The Core Feature. Create reaction panels, edit embed messages, configure forms, and set up ticket logic. Most of your time will be spent here. Commands A permission manager for slash commands. Disable specific commands (/close) or restrict them to certain roles/channels. Server Config Global settings that apply to the whole bot, such as Bot Language, Dashboard Access Roles, and Interaction Blacklists. History An audit log of all changes made via the dashboard. Useful for seeing which admin changed a setting. Statistics Visual charts showing ticket volume, claim times, and staff activity. (7 days history for Free, Unlimited for Premium). Premium Manage your subscription, view invoices, or activate a license key.

docs.title: 3. Navigation & Workflow
docs.text: The dashboard is designed for speed.

docs.title: Breadcrumbs
docs.text: Located at the top left (e.g., My Server > Support Panel > Messages). * Click My Server to go back to the server settings. * Click Support Panel to switch back to the main settings grid for that panel.

docs.title: Quick Switcher
docs.text: In the top-left of the sidebar, clicking the Server Name opens a dropdown. This allows you to jump to a different server without going back to the main menu.

docs.title: Mobile Support
docs.text: The dashboard is fully responsive. You can configure panels, edit messages, and manage subscriptions directly from your phone's browser. The sidebar collapses into a "Hamburger Menu" on smaller screens.

docs.title: 4. Saving Your Work
docs.text:
The dashboard uses a Draft System. Changes are not applied to the live bot until you explicitly save them.

Safe Save System

When you modify a setting, a Save Bar appears at the bottom of the screen.

  • Save Changes: Pushes the update to the database and the live bot.
  • Discard: Reverts all changes made since the last save.

If you try to close the tab with unsaved changes, the browser will block you with a confirmation warning.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"403 Forbidden" Error? This usually means you lost administrative access to the server, or your login session expired. -> Log Out and Log In again to refresh your permissions.

Dashboard not loading? Check our Status Page to see if the API is experiencing issues.

docs.title: Installation & Invite
docs.text: Getting TicketForge running on your server takes just a few clicks.

docs.title: 1. Invite the Bot
docs.text:
To start using TicketForge, you need to invite the bot to your Discord server and authorize it with the necessary permissions.

  • Invite TicketForge Click below to add the bot to your server. You must have Manage Server permissions. Invite Bot

docs.title: 2. Required Permissions
docs.text:
TicketForge requires specific permissions to function correctly. When inviting the bot, ensure the following permissions are granted:

Permission Reason Manage Roles To assign support roles, manage ticket permissions, and automate roles during claiming. Manage Channels To create ticket channels, rename them, and manage categories. Change Nickname To allow the bot to change its own nickname if configured. View Channels Essential for the bot to see and interact with your server's channels. Send Messages To post panels, welcome messages, and response triggers inside tickets. Send Messages in Threads Required if you use the "Tickets as Threads" feature. Create Private Threads Allows the bot to create private ticket threads for a cleaner sidebar. Manage Messages To delete and edit bot triggers/commands to keep channels clean. Pin Messages To pin ticket welcome message in the ticket channel. Manage Threads To archive/lock threads when a ticket is closed. Embed Links Necessary to send rich visual panels, buttons, and formatted logs. Attach Files Used to generate and upload HTML transcripts and audit logs. Read Message History Required to generate transcripts and view context of existing tickets. Use External Emojis Allows the bot to display custom branding and icons in its messages.

Permission Check

Ensure the TicketForge bot role is higher than the roles you select below in your server settings.

For TicketForge to manage roles (e.g., adding a "Support" role to a user), the TicketForge bot role must be higher than the role it is trying to assign in your Discord Server Settings > Roles list.

docs.title: 3. Verify Installation
docs.text: Once invited, go to a text channel in your server and type /ping. If the bot responds with "🏓 Pong!", it is successfully installed and online.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The bot is offline? Check our Status Page to see if there are any ongoing outages.

Commands not showing up? Sometimes Discord takes up to an hour to register slash commands for new bots. You can try re-inviting the bot with the link above to force a command refresh.

docs.title: Interaction Styles (Layout)
docs.text:
TicketForge offers three distinct interaction styles for your panels, allowing you to optimize for space or visual appeal.

Layout settings.

docs.title: Video Tutorial
docs.text:
Watch our video guide below to learn step-by-step how to set up both multi-panel buttons and select style (dropdown) layouts:

(If the embedded video above doesn't load, you can also watch the tutorial on YouTube.)

docs.title: 1. Single Button
docs.text: The standard panel with a single button. This is the default style and is best for simple, straightforward setups where users only need one option to click.

docs.title: 2. Select Menu (Dropdown)
docs.text:
Best for panels with many categories (e.g., "Tech Support", "Billing", "Report Player", "Bug Report").

  • Capacity: Up to 25 options in a single menu.
  • Descriptions: Each option can have a secondary text line for context.
  • Emojis: Supported for every option.
  • Logic: Each option in the dropdown triggers a different panel configuration behind the scenes.

Panel with dropdown selection.

docs.title: 3. Multi-Panel
docs.text:
A powerful layout that combines buttons from multiple different panels into a single message. Best for panels with 2-5 options.

  • How it works: You create a "Master Panel" and attach other panels to it.
  • Visual: The bot displays the buttons from all attached panels in a grid under one embed.
  • Benefit: Allows you to have a "General Support" button and an "Apply for Staff" button in the same message, even though they have completely different logic/roles behind them.

Panel with multiple buttons.

docs.title: Configurable Buttons
docs.text:
In Panel Editor > Buttons, you can customize the following system buttons for any of your panels:

Button Default Label Function Create Ticket Open Ticket Opens a new ticket for the user. Close Ticket Close Archives the ticket (or triggers confirmation). Claim Ticket Claim Assigns the ticket to the clicker. Transcript Transcript Generates a log file of the chat. Delete Delete Permanently deletes the channel. Re-Open Re-Open Moves a closed ticket back to the open category. Confirm Close Confirm The "Yes" button in the close confirmation prompt. Cancel Close Cancel The "No" button in the close confirmation prompt.
  • Customization: You can change the Label and Color (Blurple, Grey, Green, Red), and Role Requirements for each button.

docs.title: Variables & Placeholders
docs.text: You can use dynamic variables in your Messages, Embeds, and Channel Names. The bot will automatically replace them with real data when the message is sent, the channel is created, or the application is processed.

docs.title: 1. Context: User vs. Author
docs.text:
Before using variables, it is crucial to understand the difference between the User and the Author in TicketForge.

  • The User ({user_*}): The person who owns the object.
    • In a Ticket, this is the person who opened the ticket.
    • In an Application, this is the applicant.
  • The Author ({author.*}): The person who triggered the current action.
    • If the user clicks "Start Application", the user is the author.
    • If a Staff member clicks "Accept", the staff member is the author.

docs.title: 2. Application Placeholders
docs.text: These variables are specifically available within the Application Editor > Messages section (e.g., Application Received, Accepted/Denied notices).

docs.title: Application Data
docs.text: Placeholder Description {application.name} The name of the application panel (e.g., "Staff App"). {application.results} The fully formatted list of questions and answers submitted by the applicant. {application.conclusion} / {conclusion} The final status (e.g., "Accepted" or "Denied"). {application.reason} / {reason} The reason provided by staff when accepting/denying. {deadline} The calculated deadline time (if a time limit was set).

docs.title: Review & Staff Actions
docs.text:
Used in Review Results and DM Notifications.

Placeholder Description {review_action} The action in lowercase (e.g., "accepted" or "denied"). {review_action_title} The action in title case (e.g., "Accepted" or "Denied"). {review_action_time} The Unix timestamp when the review was completed. {review_reason} The sanitized reason shown on the staff review result. {application.handled_by} / {handled_by} The staff member who reviewed the application. {reviewer} Mentions the staff member who reviewed the application. {reviewer.name} The reviewing staff member's username. {reviewer.icon} URL of the reviewing staff member's profile picture.

docs.title: 3. Ticket Placeholders
docs.text: These variables are available within the Panel Editor > Messages section for standard Tickets.

docs.title: General Ticket Info
docs.text: Placeholder Description {ticket} Mentions the ticket channel (clickable link). {ticket.name} The name of the ticket channel. {ticket.id} The unique channel ID of the ticket. {ticket_opener} Mentions the user who opened the ticket. {ticket_closer} Mentions the user who closed the ticket. {close_reason} / {ticket.close_reason} The reason provided when the ticket was closed. {transcript.users} / {transcript_users} List of users involved in the ticket transcript.

docs.title: Claim Status
docs.text: Placeholder Description {claim.user} Mentions the last user who claimed the ticket. {claim.user.name} The claimer's username. {claim.user.icon} URL of the claimer's profile picture.

docs.title: Escalation Info
docs.text: Placeholder Description {escalate.reason} The reason provided for the escalation. {escalate.panel} The name of the destination panel. {escalate.staff} The staff member who escalated the ticket.

docs.title: Ticket Form Data (Pre-ticket Modals)
docs.text:
Used to extract specific answers when creating a ticket via a form.

Placeholder Description {create.form_0} The answer to the 1st question in the form. {create.form_1} The answer to the 2nd question in the form. {create.form_X} Replace X with the question index (starting at 0).

docs.title: 4. Universal Placeholders
docs.text: These variables can be used globally across both Tickets and Applications.

docs.title: User & Author Identities
docs.text: Placeholder Description {user_mention} Mentions the user/applicant (e.g. @Username). {user_name} The user/applicant's username. {user_nickname} The user/applicant's server nickname. {user_id} The user/applicant's unique Discord ID. {user_avatar} Direct URL to the user/applicant's avatar. {author} Mentions the action author (staff or user). {author.name} The author's username. {author.id} The author's unique Discord ID. {author.icon} URL of the author's profile picture.

docs.title: Server & Channel
docs.text: Placeholder Description {server.name} / {server_name} The name of the Discord server. {server.id} / {server_id} The server's unique ID. {server_members} Total member count of the server. {server.icon} Direct URL to the server's icon. {server.banner} Direct URL to the server's banner. {channel_mention} Mentions the current channel. {channel.name} / {channel_name} The name of the current channel. {channel.id} / {channel_id} The ID of the current channel.

docs.title: Time & Dates
docs.text: Placeholder Description {time} Current Unix timestamp in seconds. <t:{time}> Discord's dynamic timestamp (auto-adjusts to the viewing user's timezone). {time.created} Unix timestamp for when the ticket/app was created. {time.deleted} Unix timestamp for when the ticket/app was deleted. {time.created.age} How long ago the ticket/app was created.

docs.title: Special Variables
docs.text: Placeholder Description {empty} Inserts an empty-like invisible character. Useful for required embed fields. {random} Generates a random number (can be customized with ?rmin/?rmax modifiers). {Role ID} Pings a specific role. Replace Role ID with the actual ID (e.g., {9876543210}).

docs.title: 5. Channel Naming Specifics
docs.text:
These variables are strictly tailored for generating dynamic Ticket Channel and Thread names in the Panel settings.

Placeholder Description {user} The ticket opener's username (alias for {ticket.user.name}). {count} The unique, incrementing ticket number for this server. {panel.name} The name of the panel used to create the ticket. {panel.count} The sequential ticket number strictly for this specific panel.

docs.title: 6. Advanced Logic (Modifiers)
docs.text:
You can append modifiers to almost any variable to change how it is formatted or displayed. Syntax: {variable?modifier}

Modifier Alias Example Result / Description Uppercase ?uc {user_name?uppercase} JOHN Lowercase ?lc {user_name?lowercase} john Max Length ?ml=X {ticket.id?maxLength=5} 12345 (truncates if exceeded) Pad Left ?pl=X {count?padLeft=4} 0005 (adds leading zeros) Pad Right ?pr=X {count?padRight=4} 5000 (adds trailing zeros) Fallback ?fb=Text {claim.user?fallback=Unclaimed} Displays "Unclaimed" if variable is empty. Not Fallback ?nfb=Text {claim.user?nfb=Claimed!} Displays "Claimed!" only if the variable contains data. Math ?m=op {count?math=+1} Performs algebraic operations (+, -, *, /). Clean (None) {create.form_0?clean} Removes backticks (`) to prevent markdown breaking. Random Min ?rmin=X {random?rmin=10} Sets the minimum bound for a random number. Random Max ?rmax=X {random?rmax=100} Sets the maximum bound for a random number.

docs.title: 7. Image Placeholders Reference
docs.text:
When setting up embeds requiring Image URLs (like Thumbnails, Author Icons, or Image properties), ensure you use variables that resolve to a valid direct image URL:

  • {user_avatar}
  • {author.icon}
  • {reviewer.icon}
  • {ticket.user.icon}
  • {claim.user.icon}
  • {server.icon}
  • {server.banner}

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common issues and how to fix them.

docs.title: "Thinking..." / Interaction Failed
docs.text: The bot is not responding to button clicks. 1. Permissions: Check that TicketForge has View Channel and Send Messages in the panel channel. 2. Role Hierarchy: The bot's role must be higher than the user it is trying to manage. 3. Outage: Check our status page.

docs.title: Panel Setup Guide (Health Check)
docs.text: In the Panel Editor, click the Status Badge (e.g., "Critical" or "Healthy") in the top right. * Critical Issues: Prevent the panel from working (e.g., "No Support Roles selected"). * Warnings: Suggestions for better setup (e.g., "No Transcript Channel").

docs.title: User Can't See Ticket
docs.text:
1. Check the Category Permissions. The Category should allow the bot to Manage Permissions.
  2. Check Ticket Management > Permissions in the editor. Ensure the user isn't being removed via a "Closed Role" or "Opened Role" misconfiguration.

docs.title: Images/Avatars Not Loading
docs.text: If you uploaded a custom bot avatar and it reverted: * Ensure the file is under 8MB. * Supported formats: PNG, JPG, GIF.

docs.title: Creating a Panel
docs.text: A Panel is the interface your users interact with on Discord to open tickets. TicketForge allows you to create multiple panels for different purposes (e.g., "General Support", "Billing", "Reports").

docs.title: 1. Login & Access
docs.text:
To begin, visit the TicketForge Website.

  1. Click the Login with Discord button in the top right corner.
  2. Authorize the TicketForge application to access your account information.

The main dashboard landing page.

docs.title: 2. Server Selection
docs.text:
Once logged in, you will automatically navigate to the server selection page, here select the server where you want to create the panel.

You can also navigate to this page by clicking on your profile and then "Servers".

  1. Click on your Profile Picture in the top right corner to open the menu.
  2. Select Dashboard from the dropdown menu.

Your available servers list.
  1. You will see a list of your Discord servers:
    • Manage: The bot is already in this server. Click to enter the dashboard.
    • Invite: The bot is not in this server. Click to invite it, then refresh the page.

Can't see your server?

If a server is missing from this list, ensure you have the Manage Server permission on that Discord server. If you just got permissions, try logging out and logging back in to refresh your token.

docs.title: 3. Creating the Panel
docs.text:
After selecting a server, navigate to the Panels tab in the sidebar and click the Create New Panel card.

Click the card with the plus icon to begin.

docs.title: Step A: Selection Strategy
docs.text:
You will be presented with three ways to start your configuration:

  1. Official Templates (): Pre-configured templates designed by our team for common use cases like "General Support" or "Report Systems".
  2. Community Templates (): User-generated templates. Always review roles/permissions before using these.
  3. Import from Code (): If you have a share code (format: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX), paste it here to clone an exact configuration.

Select a template or import a code to proceed.

docs.title: Previewing Templates
docs.text:
Before making a choice, you can hover over any template card and click the Preview () button. This opens a detailed interactive preview showing exactly how the panel, forms, and messages will look in Discord.

Preview the layout and flow before selecting a template.

docs.title: Step B: Configuration
docs.text: Once a template is selected, you can configure the core identity (optional at this step) of the panel.

docs.title: Single Panel Configuration
docs.text:
For standard templates, you only need to define: * Panel Title: Internal name (e.g., "Support-Main"). * Support Roles: The Discord roles (e.g., @Moderator) that can view tickets. * Ticket Category: The Discord Category where new tickets will be created.

The setup wizard allows you to configure essential settings before launching.

docs.title: Multi-Panel Configuration
docs.text:
For complex templates (like a "Hub" system with multiple departments): 1. Select the Main (Root) panel in the sidebar to configure the entry point. 2. Select Sub-Panels to configure specific categories (e.g., "Billing"). 3. Tip: Use Copy from Main to quickly apply settings across all sub-panels.

The setup wizard allows you to configure essential settings before launching.

docs.title: Step C: Creation / Launching
docs.text:
Click Create Panel. You will be redirected to the Setup Wizard to finalize your settings (Forms, Branding, Automation) and send the panel to Discord.

The setup wizard allows you to configure essential settings before launching.

docs.title: The Panel Editor
docs.text:
The Panel Editor is your workspace for building support workflows. It features a real-time health check system, auto-save protection, and granular control over every aspect of your ticket system.

The panel eidtor screen.

docs.title: Editor Navigation
docs.text: The sidebar navigation is divided into three logical groups to help you find settings quickly:

docs.title: 1. General Ticket Options
docs.text:
Core settings that define how the ticket behaves once created.

  • General — Basic behavior like "Two-Step Close" and management roles.
  • Messages — The embed builder for Welcome messages, Panel messages, and DMs.
  • Buttons — Customize the color, label, and emoji of interaction buttons.
  • Permissions (Premium) — Configure channel visibility and role overrides.

docs.title: 2. Panel Creation Settings
docs.text:
Settings that affect how the user starts the interaction.

  • Categories — Define which Discord Category the ticket channel appears in.
  • Layout — Switch between Standard Buttons, Select Menus (Dropdowns), or Multi-Panel layouts.
  • Forms — Create modal questionnaires that users must fill out before a ticket opens.
  • Threads (Premium) — Toggle "Tickets as Threads" mode to keep your channel list clean.

docs.title: 3. Advanced Settings & Automation
docs.text:
Powerful tools for large communities and professional support teams.

  • Transcripts — Configure HTML log saving, Google Drive sync, and audit logging channels.
  • Limits — Set per-user ticket caps and operational hours (Schedules).
  • Claiming — Enable the "Claim Ticket" system for staff ownership.
  • Escalation — Configure rules for transferring tickets to other panels.
  • Automation — Auto-close on user leave and automated DM notifications.
  • Ratings — Enable the CSAT (5-star) feedback system.

docs.title: Health Check (Status Badge)
docs.text:
In the top right, you will see a live Health Status badge. * 🟢 Healthy: The panel is ready to use. * 🟡 Warning: Non-critical issues found (e.g., "No Transcript Channel selected"). * 🔴 Critical: Configuration errors that prevent the panel from working (e.g., "No Support Roles selected").

Click the badge to see a detailed checklist and "Fix" shortcuts.

See the health of your panel.

docs.title: Save System
docs.text:
The editor tracks your changes locally. If you modify a setting, a Save Bar appears at the bottom of the screen. * Discard: Reverts all unsaved changes to the last stable version. * Save Changes: Pushes your configuration to the live bot.

The savebar.

Idle Protection

If you leave the editor open without saving, an "Idle" modal will appear to prevent data loss.

docs.title: Action Menu
docs.text:
Located in the top toolbar (or under the "More" menu on mobile), these tools allow you to manage the panel itself.

The actionbar on the paneleditor page. Action Icon Description Send to Discord Posts the configured Panel Message to a text channel of your choice. Update in Discord Updates the content/embeds of an existing panel message without deleting/reposting it. Requires the Message Link. Get Code Generates a shareable code (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) to copy this configuration to another server. Clone Creates an exact duplicate of this panel within the same server. Useful for A/B testing. Template Saves this configuration as a Template (Public or Private) for future use. Rename Change the internal name of the panel (e.g., "Support" -> "Billing"). Delete Permanently removes the panel configuration. This action cannot be undone.

docs.title: Ticket Settings
docs.text:
Control the fundamental behavior of your tickets: names, permissions, and structure.

Permission settings.

docs.title: Channel Naming
docs.text:
You can define a naming pattern for your tickets.

  • Sequential: ticket-001, ticket-002
  • Username: ticket-john, ticket-sarah
  • Custom: help-{user}-{count} (Supports variables).

docs.title: Automatic Thread Creation
docs.text:
Instead of creating a text channel, you can configure the bot to create a Private Thread inside a specific parent channel.

  1. Go to Panel Editor > Threads.
  2. Enable Tickets as Threads.
  3. Parent Channel: Select the text channel where threads will spawn.

docs.title: Thread Options
docs.text:
• Add Support Team: Automatically adds all configured support roles to the thread so they can view it.
  • Allow User Invites: Allows the ticket creator to invite other users to the thread via @mention.
  • Naming: Uses the same variables as standard channels (e.g., ticket-{count}).

Permission Note

When using Threads, the "Category" settings are disabled because threads must live inside their parent channel.

docs.title: Role Permissions
docs.text: TicketForge automatically manages channel permissions so you don't have to manually set overrides.

docs.title: Opened Roles
docs.text: Select roles that should be Added or Removed from the user when a ticket is Created. * Use Case: Give the user a "Support Active" role so they show up higher in the member list.

docs.title: Closed Roles
docs.text: Select roles to modify when a ticket is Closed (Archived). * Use Case: Remove the user's ability to send messages, effectively making the channel "Read Only" for them.

docs.title: Messages & Embeds
docs.text:
TicketForge allows you to fully customize the messages sent by the bot. You can create rich, professional Embeds with images, authors, and footers using the visual builder.

The message editor screen.

docs.title: Available Triggers
docs.text: You can customize the message for every stage of the ticket lifecycle.

docs.title: Core Messages
docs.text: Trigger Description Panel Message The public message users interact with to open a ticket. Welcome Message The first message sent inside a new ticket (pings user/staff). Ticket Controls The message attached to the buttons inside an open ticket.

docs.title: Lifecycle Events
docs.text: Trigger Description Ticket Claimed Sent when a staff member claims the ticket. Ticket Unclaimed Sent when a ticket is released back to the general pool. Ticket Closed Sent when a ticket is archived/closed (replaces controls). Ticket Reopened Sent if a staff member re-opens a closed ticket. Close Confirmation Displayed when "Two-Step Close" is active (asks "Are you sure?"). Delete Warning The final warning message sent 5 seconds before channel deletion.

docs.title: Direct Messages (DMs)
docs.text: Trigger Description DM: Created Sent to the user's DMs immediately after they open a ticket. DM: Closed Sent to the user's DMs when the ticket is closed by staff.

docs.title: System & Notifications
docs.text: Trigger Description Transcript Log The message posted in your Log Channel containing the file download. Support Closed Displayed if a user tries to open a ticket outside operational hours (if enabled).

docs.title: Templates & Sharing
docs.text: Don't want to build a panel from scratch? TicketForge supports a powerful templating system that allows you to save, share, and import configurations instantly.

docs.title: Creating a Template
docs.text:
You can turn any existing panel into a template.

  1. Go to the Panel Editor for the panel you want to share.
  2. Click the Template button in the top action bar.
  3. Configure Details:
    • Title: A clear name for the setup (e.g., "Roleplay Application").
    • Description: Explain what the panel does.
    • Tags: Add tags like Support, Gaming, or Application to help others find it.
  4. Create: Once created, the template is saved to the community library.

Sensitive Data

Templates do not save server-specific IDs like Channels or Roles. When you import a template, you will need to re-map these connections.

docs.title: Importing a Template
docs.text:
When creating a new panel, you can choose Community Templates or Official Templates.

  1. Click Create New Panel.
  2. Browse the Desired (Official/Community) tab.
  3. Click Preview on a card to see the flow.
  4. Click Use Template.
  5. The Setup Wizard will guide you through mapping the required roles and categories.

docs.title: Share Codes
docs.text:
If you want to share a configuration privately without publishing it to the community list:

  1. Open the Panel Editor.
  2. Click the Code button (The Code Icon).
  3. Copy the generated Share Code (Format: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX).
  4. Give this code to another user.
  5. They can paste it into the Import Code tab when creating a panel.

Expiration

Share codes expire after 72 hours for security reasons.

docs.title: Command Management
docs.text: TicketForge offers granular control over Slash Commands. You can disable specific commands entirely or restrict them to specific channels and roles.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Navigate to the Commands tab in the sidebar. You will see a list of all available bot commands.

docs.title: Command Settings
docs.text:
Click on any command to edit its permissions:

  1. Enable Command: Master toggle. If OFF, the command acts as if it doesn't exist.
  2. Support Team Only: Restricts usage to users who have a role designated as "Support" in any of your panels.
    • Admin Commands (e.g., /setup, /purge-tickets) are restricted to Administrators automatically.

docs.title: Scope Restrictions
docs.text:
You can fine-tune where commands work:

  • Allowed Channels: The command will only work in these channels.
  • Blocked Channels: The command will work everywhere except these channels.
  • Allowed Roles: Only these roles can use the command.
  • Blocked Roles: These roles are specifically prevented from using the command.

docs.title: Available Commands
docs.text: Command Description Tickets /add <user/role> Adds a specific user or an entire role to the current ticket. /archive Transcribes the current ticket. /close <reason> Closes the current ticket with a provided reason (triggers the Close logic configured in the panel). /delete Permanently deletes the current ticket channel. /escalate <reason> Moves the current ticket to a different panel/department with a provided reason (e.g., Support -> Billing). /remove <user/role> Removes a specific user or role from the current ticket. /rename <name> Renames the current ticket channel to the specified name. /re-open Re-opens a previously closed ticket for further communication. /claim Assigns the ticket to the staff member running the command. /unclaim Releases the ticket back to the general pool by removing the assigned staff member. /priority Sets the priority level of the ticket (Low, Medium, High, Urgent). /thread Creates a private, staff-only thread within the ticket for internal discussion. Configuration /setup Launches the interactive setup wizard for creating and managing panels directly in Discord. /premium Shows the current server subscription tier, active features, and expiry date. Moderation /blacklist <username> <reason> Blacklists a user for a specific reason. If used inside a ticket, it will automatically transcribe and delete the ticket. /purge-tickets <age> Bulk deletes tickets older than the specified timeframe (Options: Everything, 24 Hours, 3 Days, 1 Week, 1 Month). General /help Displays the help menu with a comprehensive list of available commands. /ping Checks the bot's latency and Discord API response time. /invite Provides the official link to invite TicketForge to other servers. /vote Provides a link to vote for TicketForge on bot lists to earn rewards or support the bot.

docs.title: Server Configuration
docs.text:
Manage global settings that apply to the entire bot within your server.

Server Config settings.

docs.title: Bot Persona
docs.text: The Bot Persona section lets you customize how TicketForge appears in your server. There are two modes depending on your subscription plan.

docs.title: Standard Identity
docs.text:
Premium Feature

Included with the Premium Plan. Customize the bot's appearance within your server without replacing the bot application itself.

  • Nickname: Set a custom display name for the bot in your server's member list and messages.
  • Avatar: Upload a custom profile picture (PNG, JPG, or GIF, max 8MB) shown only in your server.
  • Banner: Upload a banner image displayed on the bot's profile card.
  • Bio: Set a custom "About Me" text visible when users click the bot's profile.

Leaving any of these fields blank reverts the bot to its global defaults.

docs.title: Custom Bot (Whitelabel)
docs.text:
Support Plan Exclusive

Support Plan Required

Running a full Custom Bot instance requires an active Support Plan subscription. It is not available on the Free, Trial, or Premium plans.

Take branding to the next level by running TicketForge under your own bot application. This fully replaces the "TicketForge" bot user with your own, giving you complete control over the username, avatar, and presence — the bot will appear as an entirely separate application in Discord.

  • Standard Identity (Premium)

    Customizes the bot's Nickname, Avatar, Banner, and Bio inside your server. The bot tag still shows the original TicketForge application name when clicked.

  • Full Custom Bot (Support Plan only)

    Runs a dedicated instance using your own Bot Token. Completely replaces the bot identity — your own application name, profile picture, and presence. Requires an active Support Plan.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Create a new application in the Discord Developer Portal.
  2. Enable all Privileged Gateway Intents under the Bot tab.
  3. Copy your Bot Token and paste it into the Server Config > Custom Bot section.
  4. TicketForge will spin up a dedicated instance for your server.

docs.title: Google Drive Integration
docs.text:
Premium Feature

Securely backup your transcripts to the cloud. By connecting your Google Drive, TicketForge will automatically upload HTML transcripts to a folder in your personal Drive whenever a ticket is saved.

  1. Go to Server Config > Google Drive Transcripts.
  2. Click Connect Drive.

  3. Authorize TicketForge to access your Drive files.

  4. Email: Displays the connected Google account email.

  5. Security: We use an encrypted Refresh Token system. We do not store your password.

docs.title: Dashboard Access
docs.text:
Control who can log in to the web dashboard to manage settings.

  • Administrator: Has full access by default.
  • Custom Roles: Select specific roles (e.g., "Head Mod") to grant them editor access.
    • Note: Dashboard users can see all tickets and settings but cannot manage billing.

docs.title: Server Ticket Limit
docs.text:
Cap the total number of open tickets allowed across the entire server simultaneously.

  • Enable Limit: Toggles the restriction on or off.
  • Max Open Tickets: Set the numeric maximum (e.g., 50). Once this limit is reached, users attempting to open new tickets will receive an error message until a current ticket is closed.

docs.title: Language & Localization
docs.text:
Set the default language for bot system messages.

  • Bot Language: Select your preferred language from the dropdown (e.g., English, Deutsch, Français, Español, Nederlands). This affects error messages and system prompts sent by the bot.

docs.title: Interaction Blacklist
docs.text:
Prevent abuse by blocking specific roles from interacting with the bot entirely.

  • Effect: Users with a blacklisted role cannot click buttons, use dropdowns, or run slash commands.
  • Usage: Useful for "Muted" roles or punishing users who spam tickets.
